question: What does the pairwise alignment of per-example loss gradients reveal about which examples learn together, how semantic structure emerges, and when a neural network begins to memorize rather than generalize?

key_findings.claim: The proposed stiffness is exactly a first-order pairwise interaction between example losses under a parameter update.
key_findings.evidence: For examples one and two with parameter gradients g1 and g2, an infinitesimal descent step on example one changes the second loss by minus epsilon times g1 dot g2. The paper therefore defines sign stiffness from the sign of this dot product and cosine stiffness from its normalized alignment.

key_findings.claim: Within-class and between-class gradient alignment rise or persist during feature learning and collapse toward zero after the displayed onset of overfitting.
key_findings.evidence: Across the vision experiments, same-class gradients are more aligned than cross-class gradients, and the class-aggregated curves regress toward zero late in training. Train-train, train-validation, and validation-validation measurements show qualitatively similar trajectories in the reported examples.

key_findings.claim: The CIFAR-100 stiffness matrix contains structure at semantic levels that were not explicit training targets.
key_findings.evidence: A ResNet-20 trained on the 100 fine labels has elevated gradient alignment between classes belonging to the same provided superclass. A post-hoc living-versus-nonliving grouping also exceeds the different-group baseline across the displayed training checkpoints.

key_findings.claim: A distance-conditioned zero crossing is introduced as a dynamical critical length, but it is an estimator tied to the chosen input metric and linear fit rather than an intrinsic geometric constant.
key_findings.evidence: Inputs are normalized and separated by one minus cosine similarity; within-class stiffness is binned against that raw input distance, a straight line is fitted, and its first zero crossing is called xi. The construction assumes an approximately monotone local relation and is not tested against representation-space distances or nonlinear fits.

key_findings.claim: Higher constant Adam learning rates produce smaller measured stiff regions even when runs are aligned by training loss.
key_findings.evidence: Across five rates, the displayed xi curves are ordered downward as learning rate increases both versus epoch and versus training loss. The authors interpret this as the optimizer selecting functions whose local behavior is easier to bend, not merely moving faster along the same training trajectory.

key_findings.claim: The study supplies an exploratory diagnostic, not a validated generalization estimator or a causal explanation of generalization.
key_findings.evidence: The paper does not prospectively predict held-out error, compare against generalization proxies, intervene to increase stiffness, or report calibration across seeds and hyperparameter sweeps. Its train-validation definition is a local transfer of one infinitesimal update, which is related to but not identical to the conventional train-test generalization gap.

method.core_idea: Use the Gram matrix of per-example loss gradients as a local, training-dynamics-dependent similarity map over data points.
method.mechanism: Freeze a model at selected checkpoints; compute a parameter gradient for each sampled train or validation example; form signed and cosine pairwise alignments; aggregate by class and semantic hierarchy; bin within-class alignment by normalized input cosine distance; and track these summaries over training and learning rates.
assumptions: An infinitesimal first-order update reflects interactions that matter under finite minibatch training.
Loss-gradient alignment is comparable across checkpoints despite changing gradient norms and loss saturation.
The sampled 500 or 3,000 examples represent the full pairwise structure.
Ground-truth labels do not trivially dominate the observed class and superclass alignment patterns.
Cosine distance in normalized raw input space is meaningful for the data manifold.
A linear zero crossing summarizes stiffness decay with distance.
Correlations with late overfitting carry beyond the selected architectures and optimization settings.

techniques.role: Computes a parameter-space learning direction for every audited example.
Measures whether one example's infinitesimal update helps or harms another.
Aggregates pairwise interactions into class, superclass, and broader semantic matrices.
Contrasts train-train, train-validation, and validation-validation interactions.
Relates gradient coupling to normalized raw-input cosine distance.
Defines xi from the fitted distance at which average stiffness first reaches zero.

evaluations.setting: Three-layer fully connected and convolutional networks, plus ResNet-20, on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100.
evaluations.metric: Sign and cosine gradient stiffness by split, class pair, epoch, and normalized input distance.
evaluations.result: Within-class alignment is generally strongest, cross-class alignment develops during training, and both approach zero in late displayed checkpoints associated with overfitting.
evaluations.baseline: Different class pairings and dataset splits within the same trained model; no external generalization diagnostic.

evaluations.setting: ResNet-20 trained on CIFAR-100 fine labels to approximately 60 percent top-one test accuracy.
evaluations.metric: Mean stiffness within a class, within a CIFAR-100 superclass, within a post-hoc living/nonliving group, and across groups.
evaluations.result: Alignment decreases with semantic distance and remains above the across-group baseline for the supplied higher-order groups.
evaluations.baseline: Mean alignment between classes in different semantic groups.

evaluations.metric: Within-label and between-label stiffness over fine-tuning epochs.
evaluations.result: Within-label stiffness begins positive and declines toward zero; between-label stiffness begins negative and approaches zero, qualitatively paralleling the vision curves.
evaluations.baseline: Class-aggregated vision behavior; limited task-specific quantitative reporting.

evaluations.setting: Fashion-MNIST and supplementary CIFAR-10 runs under five constant Adam learning rates.
evaluations.metric: Dynamical critical length xi versus epoch and matched training loss.
evaluations.result: Larger learning rates are associated with smaller fitted stiff-domain length at comparable training loss.
evaluations.baseline: Lower learning rates at the same reported loss rather than matched time.

limitations: Author-stated: architecture search and using stiffness as a guiding objective are only proposed as future directions.
Reviewer inference: the pairwise computation scales quadratically in sampled examples and requires per-example parameter gradients.
Reviewer inference: train-validation stiffness is a local derivative interaction, not a direct measurement or bound on the usual generalization gap.
Reviewer inference: the paper reports exploratory curves without prospective early-stopping accuracy, seed-level uncertainty, causal interventions, or standardized proxy comparisons.
Reviewer inference: the zero-crossing length depends on raw-pixel normalization, a linear fit, sampling density, class conditioning, and the chosen loss.
Reviewer inference: superclass and living/nonliving groupings are evaluated after semantic labels are known, so discovery and confirmation are not separated.
Reviewer inference: no batch normalization is used, Adam is fixed at constant rates, and the main networks and data sets are small relative to current practice.
Reviewer inference: cosine normalization discards magnitude even though magnitude determines the actual loss change under a finite update.
failure_modes: Near-zero gradients late in training make directions noisy while cosine stiffness remains numerically unstable.
Examples share a label-induced last-layer gradient and appear semantically stiff without sharing useful internal features.
A pair has positive infinitesimal alignment but a realistic finite update crosses curvature and harms the second example.
Raw input cosine distance is unrelated to perceptual or learned distance, making xi architecture- and preprocessing-dependent.
A nonmonotone stiffness-distance curve yields an arbitrary linear zero crossing.
Subsampled pair matrices miss rare harmful examples or minority-class structure.
A model generalizes under distribution shift while in-distribution pairwise stiffness gives a reassuring but irrelevant signal.
reusable_insights: Per-example gradient interactions unify local transfer, data similarity, and training-data influence in one computable object.
Gradient direction and magnitude should be reported together because they answer different intervention questions.
A generalization proxy should be judged prospectively on early stopping, model ranking, and shift prediction, not only by a visually aligned training curve.
Semantic discovery claims need held-out group definitions or unsupervised clustering before labels are inspected.
A purported critical length should be stress-tested across input, representation, and tangent-kernel metrics.
open_questions: Can sketched or layer-restricted gradients preserve the class and distance structure at modern model scale?
Does stiffness predict the best checkpoint more reliably than validation loss, margins, sharpness, or gradient-weight alignment?
Which portion of class stiffness comes from the output-label geometry versus learned shared representations?
Can training that explicitly increases selected train-validation alignments causally improve generalization?
How stable is xi under augmentations, representation-space metrics, nonlinear fits, and distribution shift?
Can the time-integral of pairwise interactions predict influence better than a single checkpoint?

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Tangent Kernel: Convergence and Generalization in Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Jacot and colleagues formalize inner products of output Jacobians as a kernel governing function evolution, with infinite-width convergence results. Stiffness uses labeled loss-gradient alignment at finite width and emphasizes empirical semantic and training-time structure rather than kernel-regime theory.

competitive_landscape.title: Sensitivity and Generalization in Neural Networks: an Empirical Study
competitive_landscape.difference: Novak and colleagues study how output sensitivity to input perturbations correlates with generalization. Stiffness instead measures sensitivity of one example's loss to a parameter update induced by another, exposing pairwise transfer and semantic grouping.

competitive_landscape.title: Gradient Similarity: An Explainable Approach to Detect Adversarial Attacks against Deep Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Charpiat and colleagues also use parameter-gradient similarity to quantify training-data influence on a test input, aimed at adversarial detection. Stiffness develops sign and cosine aggregates over training, class hierarchy, learning rate, and input distance as a generalization diagnostic.

competitive_landscape.title: Estimating Training Data Influence by Tracing Gradient Descent
competitive_landscape.difference: TracIn accumulates gradient-dot-product effects at saved checkpoints to estimate how particular training examples influence a prediction over the actual optimization trajectory. Stiffness primarily diagnoses the full pairwise geometry at individual checkpoints and does not integrate realized usage over time.

competitive_landscape.title: Input Similarity from the Neural Network Perspective
competitive_landscape.difference: Charpiat and colleagues define how a parameter variation changing one output affects another and use it for retrieval and regularization without requiring true labels. Stiffness is explicitly loss- and label-conditioned and focuses on generalization dynamics and semantic matrices.

competitive_landscape.title: TRAK: Attributing Model Behavior at Scale
competitive_landscape.difference: TRAK combines per-example gradients, random projection, normalization, and model ensembles to attribute behavior for large modern models. Stiffness retains an interpretable raw pairwise Gram geometry but has no comparable scaling or attribution validation.

competitive_landscape.title: Gradient-Weight Alignment as a Train-Time Proxy for Generalization in Classification Tasks
competitive_landscape.difference: Hölzl and colleagues align per-sample gradients with weights, construct an efficient train-time estimator, and evaluate prospective validation-free early stopping and model comparison. Stiffness provides richer example-to-example and semantic structure but lacks that direct proxy benchmark and is quadratically more expensive in sample count.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Neural-network stiffness connects per-example gradient transfer to generalization, semantic hierarchy, learning-rate implicit bias, and a dynamical critical length in input space.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper derives the pairwise loss effect and presents class matrices and training curves across four vision data sets, a fine-tuned language model, several architectures, and five learning rates.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The useful contribution is a memorable physical vocabulary and a broad empirical organization of the loss-gradient Gram matrix. Gradient and tangent-kernel similarity existed already, and later TracIn, TRAK, and gradient-weight alignment turn related signals into scalable influence or prospectively tested generalization tools. Stiffness remains best treated as an exploratory local-geometry diagnostic until its causal and predictive value is benchmarked.

reviewer_notes: Read and visually checked all 12 pages, including the supplementary class matrices and every critical-length plot. Competitors were checked at primary arXiv, NeurIPS, and PMLR records on 2026-08-23. Source lineage is direct: the reviewed bytes come from the canonical arXiv 1901.09491 route, so no identity fallback or alternate-revision substitution is involved.
